walkthroughs.body_html:
Organisms Respond to Changes — a core area of A-Level Biology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Organisms Respond to Changes brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Organisms Respond to Changes.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: The correct order of components in a simple reflex arc is:
options: receptor, sensory neurone, relay neurone, motor neurone, effector
receptor, motor neurone, relay neurone, sensory neurone, effector
effector, motor neurone, relay neurone, sensory neurone, receptor
sensory neurone, receptor, motor neurone, relay neurone, effector

mcqs.q: A woodlouse moves faster in dry air and slows in damp air, with no set direction. This response is:
options: kinesis
positive taxis
a tropism
a conditioned reflex

mcqs.q: A plant shoot growing towards a light source is showing:
options: positive phototropism
negative geotropism
a nastic response
positive hydrotropism

mcqs.q: Receptors are described as transducers because they:
options: convert the energy of a stimulus into a nerve impulse
amplify the size of the action potential
store information as a chemical memory
release hormones directly into the blood

mcqs.q: Is a spinal reflex action controlled by the brain?
options: Taxis occurs in plants while kinesis occurs in animals.
Reflexes are controlled by hormones carried in the blood.
Reflexes are quick decisions made consciously by the brain.
Most spinal reflexes are processed by relay neurones in the spinal cord, so they occur without the brain making a decision.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between taxis and kinesis?
options: Taxis occurs in plants while kinesis occurs in animals.
Taxis is directional movement toward or away from a stimulus; kinesis is a non-directional change in speed or turning rate.
The shoot grows toward light because chlorophyll is attracted to light.
Taxis and kinesis both simply mean moving away from danger.

mcqs.q: Why does a shoot grow towards light?
options: The shoot grows toward light because the light physically pulls the cells over.
The shoot grows toward light because chlorophyll is attracted to light.
Taxis occurs in plants while kinesis occurs in animals.
Auxin (IAA) accumulates on the shaded side and promotes cell elongation there, bending the shoot toward the light.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Tropism”?
options: The neurone pathway receptor to sensory to relay to motor to effector that produces a rapid, automatic, protective response without conscious thought.
A specialised cell or sensory ending that detects a specific stimulus and acts as a transducer, converting it into a nerve impulse.
A directional movement of a simple motile organism either towards (positive) or away from (negative) a directional stimulus such as light.
A growth response of a plant in which the direction of growth is determined by the direction of a stimulus, for example phototropism towards light.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Kinesis”?
options: A growth response of a plant in which the direction of growth is determined by the direction of a stimulus, for example phototropism towards light.
A detectable change in the internal or external environment of an organism that can bring about a response giving a survival advantage.
The neurone pathway receptor to sensory to relay to motor to effector that produces a rapid, automatic, protective response without conscious thought.
A non-directional response in which an organism changes its rate of movement or turning according to the intensity of a non-directional stimulus.

options: A growth response of a plant in which the direction of growth is determined by the direction of a stimulus, for example phototropism towards light.
A directional movement of a simple motile organism either towards (positive) or away from (negative) a directional stimulus such as light.
A specialised cell or sensory ending that detects a specific stimulus and acts as a transducer, converting it into a nerve impulse.
A detectable change in the internal or external environment of an organism that can bring about a response giving a survival advantage.

options: A specialised cell or sensory ending that detects a specific stimulus and acts as a transducer, converting it into a nerve impulse.
A growth response of a plant in which the direction of growth is determined by the direction of a stimulus, for example phototropism towards light.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Taxis”?
options: A growth response of a plant in which the direction of growth is determined by the direction of a stimulus, for example phototropism towards light.
A directional movement of a simple motile organism either towards (positive) or away from (negative) a directional stimulus such as light.

A specialised cell or sensory ending that detects a specific stimulus and acts as a transducer, converting it into a nerve impulse.

options: A directional movement of a simple motile organism either towards (positive) or away from (negative) a directional stimulus such as light.

Detects the stimulus and generates an impulse
Carries the impulse to the central nervous system

Carries the impulse out to the effector
Muscle or gland that produces the response
